name: v10_vec_decoder
description: fnet v10 component 5: the vector-zone instruction decoder - a SECOND ROM read at the SAME fetch address, feeding the four select/erase lines straight out of a private word 2. Proves the second read port keys off the same read_pc carrier as the instruction fetch (so one PC drives both words), that ROM2's private net makes a scalar-only slot cost nothing (word 2 reads as literally absent), and that all four bit-fields decode to their plain values through the masks the assembler generates - a drift between assembler.encode_word2 and these masks would silently select the wrong vector source, so this is where it gets caught. It also pins the asymmetry the whole design rests on: R and S are LATCHED, because a park has to persist while port A walks the bus for a lane read, while W and erase follow the word and are therefore high for exactly the tick their instruction executes - the widened-pulse bug class, gone by construction. The remaining invariant, that W lands exactly ONE tick after R/S so a commit can never capture a stale selection, is what the two mandelbrot benches assert end to end: a decoder off by one there does not produce a slightly wrong picture, it produces noise.
